title: test_checkout_total fails ~1 in 8 CI runs (SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE)
question: What makes test_checkout_total fail intermittently in CI?

hypotheses.text: Race condition between xdist workers on a session-scoped fixture
Clock/timezone dependence (datetime.now near a day boundary)
Real, unmocked network call that sometimes answers slowly or errors
Non-deterministic set/dict ordering (PYTHONHASHSEED) changes a float sum
Leftover DB state from another test that ran earlier on the same worker
Something else I am not considering

evidence.text: With 'pytest -n 0' (serial) 60/60 runs pass; with '-n 4' it fails 5/40
evidence.ref: ci-runs.csv rows 1-100 (exported from the CI UI)

evidence.text: The 40 failures are spread across all 24 hours of the day, not clustered at a day boundary
With PYTHONHASHSEED=0 fixed and '-n 4' the test still fails (3/40)
With the network blocked (pytest-socket --disable-socket) and '-n 4' it still fails (4/40)
The assert fails because order.items has 2 elements instead of 3 (one is missing), not because of a cents difference
evidence.ref: traceback of the failure in run #8812, line 'assert total == 59.97'

evidence.text: Reproducing serially with the same random order as the failure (pytest-randomly --randomly-seed=<seed of run #8812>) also fails
Changing the fixture from scope=session to scope=function removes the failures in 200 runs with '-n 4'
Running the test 500 times serially inside a single process fails at least once
